card.title: Head of Quality
card.description:
Your responsibilities
 
 
**Lead Quality Excellence in a Fast-Paced Manufacturing Environment**
We are seeking an experienced
**Head of Quality**
to lead our Quality organization and drive world-class performance across safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost objectives. This leadership role is responsible for overseeing the Quality Management System, developing quality strategies, leading customer and supplier quality initiatives, and driving continuous improvement throughout the organization.
 
 

* Lead and maintain the Quality Management System in compliance with IATF 16949 requirements.
* Develop and execute quality objectives, metrics, and improvement initiatives aligned with business goals.
* Manage customer and supplier quality activities, including audits, APQP, PPAP, launch readiness, corrective actions, and change management.
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective action efforts for internal and external quality issues.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance product quality, operational performance, and customer satisfaction.
* Monitor and report key quality metrics, including scrap, rework, and overall quality performance.
* Partner with cross-functional teams to support production, new product launches, and supplier development.
* Build, develop, and lead high-performing quality teams.

**Success Competencies**
The Head of Quality embodies the following competencies:
 
 

* Manages Complexity: Making sense of complex, high quantity, and sometimes contradictory information to effectively solve problems.
* Decision Quality: Making good and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward.
* Action Oriented: Taking on new opportunities and tough challenges with a sense of urgency, high energy and enthusiasm.
* Ensures Accountability: Holding self and others accountable to meet commitments.
* Drive Results: Consistently achieving results, even under tough circumstances.
* Develops Talent: Developing people to meet both their career goals and the organization’s goals.
* Builds Effective Teams: Building strong-identity teams that apply their diverse skills and perspective to achieve common goals.
* Communicates Effectively: Developing and delivering multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences.
* Instills Trust: Gaining the confidence and trust of others though honesty, integrity, and authenticity.
* Manages Ambiguity: Operating effectively, even when things are not certain or the way forward is not clear.
* Being Resilient: Rebounding from setbacks and adversity when facing difficult situations.

**Supervisory Responsibility:**
Directly manages the Quality Department including the Quality Engineering, Quality Systems, Quality Planning, Quality Lab/ Gauging, Change and Series Management functions.
 
 
Your profile
 
 
**Qualifications:**
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.
 
 

* Education: A Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or a related technical field is required, experience in Quality functions within the automotive industry or related areas.
* Language: Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals. Ability to write routine reports and correspondence. Ability to speak effectively before groups of customers, OEMs, or employees of organization.
* Technology: Microsoft Office Suite knowledge; SAP/ERP knowledge preferred. Knowledge of IATF 16949, APQP-PPAP, FMEA, MSA, 8D, Statistics, GD&T and mechanical manufacturing processes.
* Travel: Occasional travel, up to 10% including international

The [above] is intended to describe the general content of and requirements for the performance of this job. It is not to be construed as an exhaustive statement of duties, responsibilities, or requirements. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
 
 
Your benefits
 
 

* Annual Bonus Eligibility of 6% of your base salary!
* 10% Shift Premium, based on base wage
* Perfect Attendance Bonus; $2,600 Minimum Annual Potential!
* Performance Productivity Bonus, $2,600 Minimum Annual Potential!
* Paid Time Off (PTO)
* Supplier Discounts
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Paid Company Holidays
* Medical, Dental, Vision, Prescription Drug Coverage
* Exclusive free medical services through our partnership with Marathon Health for employees and their dependents 3+ years of age.
* 401(K) Plan with 5% Company match!

**Company**
thyssenkrupp Dynamic Components is one of the world’s automotive industry leading partners for development and manufacturing of highly complex, state-of-the-art drivetrain technologies for both combustion engines and electric motors. Worldwide, 10 locations with 3,800 employees produce over 25 million drivetrain components per year. The product portfolio includes camshafts and cylinder head cover modules for the valve train as well as rotor shafts for battery electric vehicles.
 
 
Our electrical A/C compressor, designed for the natural refrigerant CO2, sets new standards in efficient and sustainable thermal management.
 
 
With precision and passion, we are enabling our customers in the automotive industry to achieve their emission and sustainability targets for more than 30 years.
 
 
thyssenkrupp Presta Dynamic Components is proud to be Certified by
**Great Place To Work**
. The prestigious award is based entirely on what current employees say about their experience working at thyssenkrupp Presta Dynamic Components. This year, 82% of employees said it’s a great place To Work – 25 points higher than the average U.S. company. Great Place To Work is the global authority on workplace culture, employee experience, and the leadership behaviors proven to deliver market-leading revenue, employee retention and increased innovation.
 
 
Contact
 
 
We only accept online applications submitted through the 'Apply Now' button on this job posting. You can find all current job openings on our career site at: https://jobs.thyssenkrupp.com/en Thank you for your interest in joining our team!
 
 
**Notices:**
Job Applicant Notice of Collection

card.title: Senior Director, CMC-Lead and Product Stewardship, Global Technical Operations
card.description:
**Location** Gaithersburg, Maryland, United States **Job ID** R-264447 **Date posted** 16/11/2026

 

**Introduction**

As Senior Director, CMC Product Lead and Head of Product Stewardship, you will lead end-to-end CMC product strategy and the Product Stewardship and Product Champion organization within Global Technical Operations (GTO).

You will lead sophisticated Global CMC programs across development, PPQ, commercialization, and lifecycle management while shaping Product Stewardship capabilities, governance, processes, and talent.

You will guide strategy, manage risk, and drive cross-functional decisions that support product progression and commercial supply.

**What you'll do**

You will lead global CMC operations groups for sophisticated biologics and other advanced modalities across development, PPQ, market rollout, and end-to-end product stewardship. You will define and deliver Global CMC strategies across manufacturing science and technology, manufacturing, analytical, quality, regulatory, technical transfer, and supply activities.

You will lead all aspects of the responsibilities related to Product Stewardship and the role of Product Champion, improving technical and CMC leadership throughout the product lifecycle. Working with BPD, Cross-SET, eGPT, GPT, and Operations teams, you will shape product strategy, influence decisions, and resolve cross-functional issues. Ensure products and processes are scalable, robust, transferable, and ready for commercialization and lifecycle management.

You will advance Early Engagement and drive CoGS strategy, identifying risks early and incorporating yield, process efficiency, manufacturability, network fit, and supply resilience into product decisions. You will also strengthen post-launch CMC leadership across product quality, supply, lifecycle improvements, and post-approval submissions.

You will establish effective governance, decision rights, escalation pathways, role clarity, and ways of working. You will lead all aspects of sophisticated product, technical, quality, supply, and CMC issues and represent Operations, Biologics, and GTO in senior governance discussions.

You will champion data-driven decision-making and the practical use of digital tools, sophisticated analytics, automation, and AI-enabled capabilities. You will build organizational strength through talent development, succession planning, and an inclusive, high-performing culture.

**Essential requirements**

* Degree in a relevant scientific or engineering field.
* 15+ years of leadership experience in the biopharmaceutical industry, with deep expertise in biologics, CMC, technical operations, commercialization, product stewardship, or related fields.
* Experience leading sophisticated Global CMC programs, Operations Global CMC teams, major biologics products, or comparable cross-functional technical programs.
* Strong understanding of late-stage development, scale-up, technology transfer, process validation and PPQ, commercialization, control strategy, comparability, lifecycle management, and post-approval change.
* Proven track record to align cross-functional teams within a global matrix.
* Experience leading senior technical teams and building organizational capability through talent development and succession planning.
* Strong enterprise and matrix leadership, with the credibility to influence decisions in senior governance forums.
* Excellent communication and judgment, with the ability to explain complex issues clearly and connect technical decisions with product and business outcomes.

**Desirable requirements**

* Advanced degree in a relevant scientific or engineering field.
* Experience leading Product Stewardship, Product Champion, technical product leadership, or similar product-facing organizations.
* Experience across development and commercial manufacturing networks, including internal and external supply.
* Experience with Global CMC governance, regulatory submissions, post-approval changes, and lifecycle management for biologics or complex modalities.
* Experience advancing digital transformation, analytics, automation, or AI-enabled capabilities within CMC, MSAT, Product Stewardship, or manufacturing operations.
* Experience crafting or improving cross-functional processes, frameworks for authority and accountability, and operating models in a global organization.

**Why AstraZeneca?**

At AstraZeneca, we 're dedicated to being a Great Place to Work. Where you are empowered to push the boundaries of science and spark your entrepreneurial spirit. There’s no better place to make a difference to medicine, patients and society. An inclusive culture that champions diversity and collaboration, and always committed to lifelong learning, growth and development. We’re on an exciting journey to pioneer the future of healthcare.

*The annual base pay for this position ranges from $216,996.00-$325,494.00*

*Our positions offer eligibility for various incentives—an opportunity to receive short-term incentive bonuses, equity-based awards for salaried roles and commissions for sales roles. Benefits offered include qualified retirement programs, paid time off (i.e., vacation, holiday, and leaves), as well as health, dental, and vision coverage in accordance with the terms of the applicable plans.*

 

#LI-Hybrid

**Date Posted**

17-Nov-2026

**Closing Date**

30-Nov-2026

Our mission is to build an inclusive environment where equal employment opportunities are available to all applicants and employees. In furtherance of that mission, we welcome and consider applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of their protected characteristics. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please complete the corresponding section in the application form.

card.title: Director, Product Operations
card.description:
**We're looking for a**

**Director, Product Operations**
================================

**This role is** **Hybrid, Dublin Office**

The **Director, Product Operations** is a senior leader who improves how the product development organization makes decisions and turns strategy into results. This role strengthens portfolio planning and execution while connecting product investments to customer and business outcomes.

Working across functions and through influence, the Director brings clarity to complex choices, aligns senior stakeholders, and drives accountability for outcomes. The role helps leaders make timely tradeoffs, improves execution predictability, and ensures product investments deliver measurable value.

**\*\*Preference for candidate who can be hybrid in Dublin, CA or Santa Monica, CA or New York office**

**In this role you will…**
--------------------------

### **Product Operating Model and Operational Rigor**

* Establish and continuously improve the product operating model, including planning cycles, portfolio and roadmap reviews, decision forums, product performance reviews, and post-launch learning loops, with a focus on improving decision quality, speed, accountability, and measurable outcomes.
* Create integrated visibility into priorities, milestones, dependencies, capacity, risks, decisions, and commitments across the product portfolio.
* Drive disciplined follow-through on decisions and actions, surfacing tradeoffs and gaps early and ensuring accountable owners are aligned.

### **Portfolio Strategy and Investment Planning**

* Partner with Product, Engineering, and Finance leaders to translate company and product strategy into a balanced, executable portfolio of investments.
* Implement a horizon-based planning approach that balances near-term customer and commercial commitments, core product and platform health, and longer-term growth and innovation.
* Connect portfolio choices to expected customer, product, operational, and financial outcomes, with clear assumptions, capacity implications, dependencies, and risks.

### **Product Intelligence and Executive Decision Support**

* Integrate customer feedback, product usage, market signals, delivery performance, and financial data to identify trends, evaluate portfolio performance, and inform product decisions.
* Provide senior leaders with concise, data-driven insights and recommendations that frame portfolio choices, investment tradeoffs, performance gaps, and decisions requiring leadership action.
* Translate complex and sometimes conflicting inputs into clear options, implications, and recommended actions that improve decision quality and accelerate alignment.

### **Delivery Success and Value Realization**

* Partner with Product and Engineering leaders to establish measurable success criteria and outcome targets before major investments and roadmap commitments are approved.
* Promote delivery practices that prioritize customer value, adoption, retention, quality, supportability, and business impact over feature output alone.
* Identify barriers to value realization and coordinate the cross-functional actions needed to improve enablement, readiness, adoption, product performance, or customer outcomes.

**You have what it takes if…**
------------------------------

* 8+ years of progressive experience in Product Operations, Product Management, Business Operations, Strategy, Program Management, Finance, or a related function within a complex technology or SaaS organization.
* Demonstrated success establishing or scaling product planning, portfolio management, governance, analytics, or operating rhythms across Product and Engineering organizations.
* Experience guiding portfolio prioritization and investment tradeoffs across customer, strategic, technical, operational, and financial needs.
* Strong understanding of product development lifecycles, roadmap planning, release execution, adoption, and post-launch value realization.
* Demonstrated ability to use customer, product, operational, market, and financial data to influence priorities and decisions.

card.title: Director of Technical Operations (Audio-Visual)
card.description:
Visual Sound is seeking a highly experienced and strategic leader to serve as the company's **Director of Technical Operations.** This (onsite) role involves overseeing the day-to-day operations to ensure a seamless workflow, drive operational excellence, and align technical initiatives with business objectives.

The Director of Technical Operations should possess strong management skills, a tactical mindset, and the ability to balance strategic oversight with hands-on operational leadership. This role also requires the capacity to streamline processes and manage teams successfully to ensure efficient processes and sustainable growth.

While a technical background in A/V is required, this person must also be proficient in supervising others, procedures, budgeting, and putting proposals together.

**Responsibilities:**

* Lead and develop high-performing teams, drive accountability, and foster collaboration across departments.
* Setting and executing operational strategies, scaling operations, and using KPIs for data-driven decision-making.
* Workflow improvements, cost reduction, and ensuring smooth day-to-day operations.
* P&L management, budgeting, cost control, and financial forecasting.
* Implementing new systems, restructuring teams, and improving company-wide efficiencies.
* Performance reporting and analysis of ongoing operations
* Familiarity with a similar operational environment is a plus.

**Previous Experience:**

* People management & leadership
* Strategic thinking & execution
* Process optimization & operational excellence
* Financial & budget management
* Change management & adaptability

card.title: Director of Operations
card.description:
The Director of Operations leads all day-to-day operations at Innova's M3 facility in Mexicali, Mexico, including production, maintenance, purchasing, shipping and receiving, and site safety. Working closely with the site leadership team, this role ensures production goals, quality standards, cost targets, and customer delivery commitments are met. The Director builds and develops a strong local team, drives continuous improvement, and serves as the key link between the Mexicali plant and Innova's U.S. leadership, Finance, Quality, and Sales teams. The ideal candidate is based in the San Diego area, is fully bilingual in English and Spanish, and has proven experience leading manufacturing operations in Mexico.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Champion and uphold the company's values, mission, and quality policy in all activities.

* Adhere to and help enforce company policies, procedures, and internal control standards.

* Ensure compliance with all applicable Quality Management System (QMS) requirements, including ISO 9001 and ISO 13485, as applicable to this role.

* Follow all safety rules and PPE requirements, and promptly report hazards, incidents, and near-misses.

* Lead all operations at the M3 facility, including production, maintenance, purchasing, and shipping and receiving, to meet production goals, quality standards, and customer delivery commitments.

* Direct and develop the site leadership team, including hiring, training, performance management, and succession planning.

* Oversee production planning and scheduling to balance capacity, labor, and materials with customer demand.

* Establish operational KPIs and monitor productivity, efficiency, scrap, cost, and on-time delivery, taking corrective action as needed.

* Oversee the site safety program and ensure compliance with applicable Mexican health, safety, and environmental regulations (e.g., STPS and NOM standards), fostering a strong culture of safety.

* Develop and manage the site operating budget, labor plan, and capital expenditure requests.

* Oversee equipment maintenance and facility upkeep to maximize uptime and maintain a safe, organized plant.

* Drive lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives to reduce waste, improve throughput, and lower costs.

* Coordinate with logistics and customs partners to support cross-border shipments, materials flow, and import/export requirements.

* Partner with Human Resources on workforce planning, employee relations, and compliance with Mexican labor law.

* Serve as the primary liaison between the Mexicali plant and Innova's U.S. leadership, Quality, Finance, and Sales, providing regular operational and financial reporting.

* Perform other related duties as required.

**EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE**

* Bachelor's degree in Operations Management, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field, required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, including at least 5 years in a leadership role, required.

* Experience leading manufacturing operations in Mexico (maquiladora or similar cross-border environment) strongly preferred.

* Experience with plastics manufacturing processes (e.g., injection molding, thermoforming, CNC machining) preferred.

* Lean Manufacturing or Six Sigma certification preferred.

**SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS**

* Fully bilingual in English and Spanish (written and verbal) required.

* Proven leadership skills, with the ability to build, motivate, and develop a high-performing team.

* Extensive knowledge of manufacturing operations, production planning, and plant management.

* Strong working knowledge of lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies.

* Financial acumen, with the ability to develop budgets, manage costs, and interpret financial data.

* Working knowledge of Mexican labor, safety, and environmental regulations.

* Working knowledge of quality system requirements under ISO 9001 and ISO 13485, as applicable to this role.

* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and ERP/MRP systems.

* Valid passport and ability to cross the U.S.–Mexico border regularly.

**TRAINING & COMPETENCY REQUIREMENTS**

* Complete new-hire orientation and role-specific on-the-job training prior to performing unsupervised work.

* Complete Quality Management System (QMS) training applicable to this role, including quality policy awareness and the consequences of nonconformance to product or process requirements.

* Complete safety training applicable to this role (e.g., PPE use, lockout/tagout, forklift certification).

* Maintain competency through periodic refresher or retraining as required by department procedures and applicable regulatory requirements.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**

* Office setting.

* Manufacturing floor environment.

* Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) such as safety glasses.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

* Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer.

* Mobility to navigate the production floor to conduct inspections and oversight.

**EXPECTED HOURS OF WORK**

* This is a full-time exempt position, required to work Monday through Friday. Occasional weekend availability may be required based on business needs.

**TRAVEL**

* Regular cross-border travel between San Diego, CA and the M3 facility in Mexicali, with on-site presence required a minimum of 4 days per week.

* Occasional travel to other Innova facilities, customers, and suppliers, up to 10%.

Pay: $110,000.00 - $150,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person
